pensamiento:
I'm checking the second user story against the quality criteria. It names an agency user with a clear action and benefit, so that part passes. It bundles historical FA and FPDS data for the FABS go-live, which could be one objective or two separate sources, and I'm weighing whether it should be split.

I'm going through the remaining criteria now. The second story's wording is arguably one objective or two separate data loads, so splitting it is still open, but I'm holding off on that until I see whether there are other defects. The benefit on the fourth story reads as a real value, though vague. The fifth story avoids prescribing a technical solution. The sixth story is the clearer problem: "all necessary columns" and "correct and complete" have no concrete measure, so it fails.

I'm checking the historical FPDS loading story against CTX-FS-090, a spike on the best way to load that data, which is related but doesn't contradict it, so it passes. The Developer loader story for CTX-FS-071 has a different role and benefit, so it isn't a duplicate. The backlog uses the same English phrasing across its stories, so the uniform format holds. For independence, the FABS go-live timing is an implicit link to the FABS production deployment and possibly to the loader and spike stories, which I'm still weighing as an unnamed dependency.

I'm weighing whether the FPDS feed and the FABS go-live are dependencies that should be named, since the story relies on the historical FPDS loader and go-live timing without referencing them. I'm also checking whether the story is estimable, because "all historical FA data," "all necessary columns," and the time period are left undefined, so it doesn't meet that criterion either. Smallness is what I'm turning to next.

I'm checking the sixth story's "all necessary columns" and "correct and complete" without a measure, and the fifth and first criteria for acceptance and business rules. Acceptance criteria are missing entirely, so verifiability fails, and the undefined columns, time range and error cases leave the business rules unclear. The historical volume may also call for stated performance or volume limits, which I'm still weighing.

I'm checking the historical load of FA and FPDS data against the remaining criteria. It's high volume, so the lack of any stated volume or performance expectation is a minor gap. Several other defects are piling up, so this will likely go back for revision, and I'm pulling the estimation and cross-reference details next.

pensamiento:
I'm estimating this story at 8 or 13 points by comparison with similar data loads. The description doesn't give a scope I can measure, so I'm weighing whether to call it 8 with a note or to register a 1, since the rule says a 1 applies when the scope can't be estimated.

I'm weighing the 8 estimate against 13, and going with 8 with a note that it's provisional until the scope is clarified. I'm also deciding that the story gets a devolver decision and listing the defects, including QUS-002, since the FA and FPDS loads could be delivered separately.

I'm checking whether the FPDS loader dependency (CTX-FS-090) counts as unplanned work, and I'm leaving that under DOR-001 rather than INV-001. The estimate of 8 meets the size limit, so INV-004 passes. For a devolver I'll leave the acceptance criteria empty and keep the refined user story short, without adding scope.

I'm settling on the form of the decision now: a devolver, with the Spanish wording for the user story and the type set to functional, and I'm checking the estimation tool before going further.

recomendaciones.texto: La HU pide dos cargas distintas (Financial Assistance y FPDS históricos). Confirmar si son un solo objetivo; si pueden entregarse por separado, separarlas en dos HU o justificar por qué van juntas.

Reemplazar los términos vagos: 'all necessary columns' debe listar las columnas o referirse a una especificación concreta, y 'correct and complete' debe expresarse como reglas de validación verificables (por ejemplo, conteos o reconciliación contra la fuente).

Precisar el alcance para estimar: periodo histórico a cargar (desde qué año), fuentes exactas, volumen aproximado y si incluye las derivaciones de FREC mencionadas en otra HU del backlog (CTX-FS-051).

Agregar criterios de aceptación en forma de reglas o lista de verificación con resultados observables, por ejemplo: qué registros deben quedar cargados, qué validación de completitud se ejecuta y qué ocurre si una carga falla.

Nombrar las dependencias: el go-live de FABS (CTX-FS-040), el cargador histórico de FPDS (CTX-FS-071) y la decisión de cómo cargar FPDS desde 2007 (CTX-FS-090), y de qué sistema o equipo se obtienen los datos fuente.
Definir las reglas de negocio de la carga: rango de fechas, columnas obligatorias, validaciones y qué hacer con registros que fallen la validación o casos de error.
Declarar requisitos no funcionales medibles para una carga de alto volumen, por ejemplo tiempo máximo de ventana de carga, volumen esperado de registros y tolerancia a fallos o reintentos.
